essence: Of things no arising; naturally they shine by your contemplation, even the non-true borrowing momentary truth. This universe-glory is will-born from you, birth from elsewhere denied; hence you shine in worlds — one, yet many-selfed. Nonduality without cancelling multiplicity: one, yet many-selfed.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at one, yet many-selfed. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual self-manifestation — the Absolute shining in worlds without being divided.
